- Experimental Fairness: Reviewer questioned whether GoalRank’s success was due to the model architecture or simply because it was trained using a more powerful Reward Model than the evaluators used by the baseline
- Baseline Strength: Reviewers noted a lack of comparison with modern single-stage large ranking models (specifically RankMixer) and contemporary retrieval-ranking unified methods like Onerec
- Operational Practicality: Multiple reviewers expressed concern that a monolithic large model would incur prohibitive training costs and high online latency compared to modular multi-stage systems
- Adaptability: Reviewers were concerned that a single generator model would be less flexible than a modular "Generator-Evaluator" system when business objectives

reviewer_concerns.value:
Concerns Addressed:

• Fairness and Reward Models: The authors clarified that all baselines and GoalRank used the exact same frozen evaluator in both offline and online tests, ensuring the performance lift is architectural.

• Stronger Baselines: The authors added RankMixer (CIKM 2025) as a baseline. GoalRank significantly outperformed it (e.g., 69.93 vs 49.72 H@6 on Industry data), proving that its list-wise generation architecture is superior to recent point-wise large models.

• Efficiency Metrics: The authors provided hard production logs showing GoalRank is faster than the production multi-stage pipeline and has a significantly higher Model Flops Utilization, debunking the "prohibitive cost" concern.

Outstanding Concerns:

• Diversity of One-Stage Baselines: While RankMixer was added, some specific retrievers mentioned by Reviewer t9JT (Onerec/Tiger) were not compared directly, though the authors argued that list-wise re-ranking baselines were more task-compatible.

• Long-Term Objective Shift: While the authors proposed a "fusion strategy" for online goal-switching, a major fundamental change in ranking philosophy might still require a more complex retraining than a modular evaluator swap.
